title: All-providers-failed data errors reach panels as raw Python exception strings, with no 'what would unlock it'
repro: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/ZZZQNOPE -> 502 {"detail":"yfinance quote failed for 'ZZZQNOPE': 'PriceHistory' object has no attribute '_dividends'"}; the Equity Overview / Watchlist / Chart panels print that string verbatim
notes: spec Edge-Cases-Pass-B promises an honest 'unavailable' + reason + what would unlock it. D43's humanizer (services/errors.py) covers LLM errors only; ProviderError has a `kind` taxonomy but the global handler ignores it. Smallest fix: map ProviderError.kind -> {message, action} in the app.py handler (reuse errors.HumanError shape) and have panels render message+action with raw detail behind the existing toggle.

title: Portfolio market value / P&L carry no freshness badge — stale or after-hours quotes read as live
repro: design: open Portfolio after IN close (or with a Yahoo-throttled stale quote); value + P&L render with no live/EOD/stale label while Watchlist shows one for the same quote
evidence: src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:140-166 (quotes fetched, only fetch failure badged), src/modules/watchlist/WatchlistPanel.tsx:75 (badge exists elsewhere), sidecar/services/locale.py:225-254
notes: spec Edge-Cases + FR-041: stale/after-hours data never shown as live. The Quote already carries `freshness`; smallest fix = reuse StalenessBadge per row + a summary-level 'as of' on the totals.

title: Native web search has no per-RUN cap off-Anthropic and per-search billing is never metered
repro: design: tier_a + a native-search model on OpenAI/Gemini/xAI/OpenRouter -> opts['web_search_max_uses'] is popped by the adapter; the loop counter only counts the local `web_search` tool, which is withheld on the native tier
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1335-1340,1416,1553-1561; sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:664-667; sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:110-112; sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:109-113 (comment promises a loop-level counter that is not there); sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:82-84; src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:921
notes: spec Edge-Cases (FR-081): per-run search cap + legible cost-so-far. Anthropic cap is per request (x6 rounds). BudgetGuard prices tokens only, so a $10/1k-search lane is invisible to the spend ceiling and the UI. Smallest fix: count native searches from adapter usage/citation metadata per round, stop sending web_search=True once the run total hits the cap, add a per-search rate to model_registry prices and surface it in cost().

title: yfinance is still the de-facto India primary for fundamentals/statements/analyst
repro: design: provider_registry candidates for model_key='fundamentals', region IN = openbb-mcp (all-null shells for IN, D72) -> yfinance; no exchange-direct / filing-derived fundamentals provider exists
notes: spec Edge-Cases-Pass-B: 'yfinance is never the trusted India primary'. Holds for quote/OHLC only. D73 proved yfinance is 'present-but-subtly-off' below mid-cap (141x institutional holding, promoter drift). Cross-checks flag some fields but the primary number shown is still yfinance's. Likely overlaps the data-battery sweeps — merge there. Fix shape: an exchange/XBRL-derived IN fundamentals provider ranked above yfinance for the fields it can serve.
